text:
caroline: thinking about prefill strategy — coordinator that instructs nodes to prefill vs letting each node decide. tradeoffs?

ravi: coordinator gives global fairness and avoids duplicate prefetch load spikes. single point + complexity though.

tim: local decisions are simpler and lower latency but can duplicate prefetches and thrash eviction. we saw that in last canary. :grimacing:

jess: can we do soft coordinator — local decides mostly, coordinator only for heavy tenants/hot prefixes?

eviction-bot: alert: prefill-spike detected on shard-12 at 03:12 UTC (sampled 87s)

ravi: hybrid seems promising. coordinator issues lease tokens for high-load prefixes; locals respect tokens if present, otherwise greedy local prefill.

caroline: question: how do we preserve read-after-write atomicity? if local prefill reads stale data while coordinator migrates ownership...

tim: we should tie token to epoch + generation; prefill must check lease epoch before committing cache residency. pattern: if epoch mismatch, abort prefill.

jess: sketch of API: 
```
request_prefill(prefix, shard_hint, if_epoch=E) -> {ok, lease_token?}
```

ravi: also need metrics: prefill_conflicts, coordinator_fallbacks, duplicate_prefill_count. run canary with chaos testing.

caroline: action items: 1) draft RFC for hybrid prefill coordinator with lease epochs (owner: caroline) 2) add metrics and a simple simulation (owner: tim) 3) run tenant-chaos test (owner: jess). agreeable?

tim: +1

jess: +1 :rocket:

ravi: +1. adding doc link: https://redwood.local/rfc/prefill-hybrid

caroline: cool — I'll put a short design doc in the RFC and post here when ready.
